smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-01.title: Count by smallest digit
smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-01.body:
Consider all strings $000$ to $999$ (those below $100$ contain a leading $0$, so they contribute $0$ and do not change the sum). The sum of $p$ equals $\sum_{d\ge1}\#\{\text{strings with all digits}\ge d\}=\sum_{d=1}^{9}(10-d)^3=9^3+8^3+\dots+1^3=2025$.

**Answer: 2025**

smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-02.title: Product formula
smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-02.body:
$f(n)=\sigma(n)/n$, and for squarefree $n=p_1\cdots p_k$ this equals $\prod\frac{p_i+1}{p_i}$. Let $P$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. For $f(n)$ to be an integer, $P$ must divide $\prod(p_i+1)$. $P\nmid P+1$, and for $p_i<P$ we have $p_i+1\le P$, so $P\mid p_i+1$ forces $p_i+1=P$: consecutive primes, so $p_i=2$, $P=3$. Hence $n\in\{1,2,3,6\}$.

$f(1)=1$, $f(2)=\frac32$, $f(3)=\frac43$, $f(6)=\frac32\cdot\frac43=2$. Only $n=6$ works.

**Answer: 1**

smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-03.title: Recurrence by last animals
smt-2012-advanced-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $a_n$ = ways ending in a bear, $b_n$ = ending in exactly one cat (preceded by a non-cat), $c_n$ = ending in two cats, $d_n$ = ending in a dog. Then $a_n=b_{n-1}+c_{n-1}+d_{n-1}$, $b_n=a_{n-1}+d_{n-1}$, $c_n=b_{n-1}$, $d_n=a_{n-1}+b_{n-1}+c_{n-1}+d_{n-1}$, starting from $(1,1,0,1)$ at $n=1$. Iterating to $n=7$ gives $(276,250,95,381)$, total $1002$.

**Answer: 1002**
